14
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the November 24, 2006/Agrahayana 3, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Agro and Rural Industries; Chemicals and Fertilizers;
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests;
Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Small Scale Industries; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
Cheating consumers through
advertisements
†*41. SHRI SHATRUGHAN SINHA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the cases of cheating of consumers through
attractive but illusive advertisements;
(b) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to ban such advertisements;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
constitute a National Consumer Protection
Regulatory Authority in this regard;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, whether Government propose
to consider any such suggestion?
Agricultural products' outlets at
stations
†*42. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether agriculture products' outlets
are being set up at railway stations;
(b) if so, the details of services and
facilities that would be made available at
these outlets;
(c) whether farmers would be benefited
by these outlets; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Pollution in Delhi
†*43. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
 (a) whether it is a fact that due to
pollution at many places in Delhi, the
atmosphere has become adverse for human
life;
(b) if so, in addition to ITO and Chandni
Chowk, the names of the places where due
to pollution the atmosphere has become
adverse for human life; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

15
(c) whether Government have traced the
reasons for pollution of the atmosphere
and if so, the details thereof?
Ganga Action Plan
*44. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
 (a) what were the objectives of the
Ganga Action Plan and the schedule of its
implementation;
(b) the total amount spent over this
project and the foreign aid component
therein;
(c) whether the Plan has been able to
achieve the stated objectives; if not, the
reasons therefor;
(d) whether it is a fact that serious
questions have been raised on the efficacy
of the project; and
(e) the steps being taken to control the
pollution in the river?
Forest clearances on fast track
*45. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
 (a) whether Government have put in
place a new policy and system to "FAST-
TRACK" all the forest clearances;
(b) how many forest clearances have
been given in Southern States in the last
two years, State-wise;
(c) out of such forest clearances, how
many were cleared under the "FAST-
TRACK" forest clearance facility;
(d) whether a system of incentives has
been offered to various officials in the
Southern region to help to bring all
applications under "FAST-TRACK" ambit;
and
(e) the details of "FAST-TRACK"
forest clearances and their negative impact
on forests?
Agriculture reform scheme
†*46. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
 (a) whether Government are
considering to implement necessary
agriculture reform scheme keeping in view
the tendency of suicides by farmers in the
country; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reform programmes to be included in this
regard?
Controlling dengue and
chikungunya
*47. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH  AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
 (a) the number of dengue and
chikungunya cases reported in the Capital
during the last three months;
(b) the number of patients suffering
from these diseases and actually admitted
in Government hospitals in the Capital and
how many of them died during that period;
(c) whether Government hospitals in the
Capital were not fully equipped to handle
such cases and a large number of patients
had to rush to private hospitals and incurred
heavy expenses which were beyond the
reach of many such patients; and
(d) the remedial steps Government
propose to take to handle such a situation
in future?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

16
NCF recommendations
†*48.SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
 (a) whether all the reports of the
National Commission on Farmers have been
received by Government;
(b) if so, when;
(c) the details of the recommendations
of the Commission and by when
Government would take a decision on them;
(d) whether it is a fact that one of the
members of the Commission has given his
own suggestions due to his disagreement
on some of the recommendations of the
Commission; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and the
reaction of Government

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the November 24, 2006/Agrahayana 3, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Agro and Rural Industries; Chemicals and Fertilizers;
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests;
Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Small Scale Industries; Steel)
Total number of questions — 155
Reducing cost  of sunflower seeds
244. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that sunflower
seeds producing companies are selling their
products at Rs. 500 to Rs. 600 per 2 kg.
packets based on their brand names;
(b) if so, the estimated cost of producing
the seeds and profit margins enjoyed by
the manufacturers;
(c) the methodology adopted for fixing
prices and the authority which is fixing
prices of all hybrid variety seeds; and
(d) whether there is any proposal by
Government to reduce the cost of sunflower
seeds and other hybrid seeds to mitigate
the problems of farmers?
Suicides vis-a-vis loans from private
money lenders
245. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the reports of continuous farmers’ suicides
from various States;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the loan with
exorbitant interest rates taken from the
private money lenders is one of the major
causes for the distress of farmers;
(d) if so, whether Government have
taken any measure to protect the farmers
who are indebted to the money lenders;
(e) whether Government would declare
the debts taken from the money lenders as
illegal; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Liberalising trade in agriculture
commodities
246. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY :
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to liberalise the trade in agricultural
commodities;
(b) the reasons which forced
Government, hitherto, not to liberalise the
said trade;
(c) the impact of this decision on the
prices of agricultural commodities;

59
(d) whether it is not a fact that the recent
price rise is the result of the above decision;
and
(e) if so, whether Government  would
review the said decision?
MSP of wheat
247. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Minimum
Support Price (MSP) of wheat has been
raised by Rs. 100/- per quintal;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that,
considering the rising cost of fertilizers,
agricultural implements and labour, the
MSP fixed is very low; and
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto?
Subsidies to farmers for increasing
wheat production
248. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal under
Government's consideration to offer liberal
subsidies to the farmers in the country to
substantially increase production of wheat
during the ensuing rabi season; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Setting up of National Agricultural
and Technology Mission
249. DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO : Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a National
Agricultural and Technology Mission is
being proposed to be set up to revive the
farm sector;
(b) if so, the details of the mandate,
power and functions of the said mission;
(c) to what extent, it would be different
from the existing National Commission on
Farmers; and
(d) the details of strategy to strengthen
farm sector and overcome farmers' suicide?
Increasing investment in agriculture
250. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether FAO of the United Nations
has called for greater investment in
agriculture and policy support for evolving
public-private partnership in agriculture as
over 854 million people, a  large number of
them in India itself, are destined to go
hungry;
(b) if so, whether according to the
report, 40 countries including India are
facing food shortage;
(c) if so, whether Government have
examined the report; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take to meet the situation?
NCF recommendations
251. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Commission
on Farmers, headed by Dr. M.S.
Swaminathan had submitted its final report;
(b) if so, whether the report has
suggested for setting up a National Food
Security and Sovereignty Board under the
Chairmanship of the Prime Minister;

the Commission;
(d) by what time a National Policy for
Farmers is likely to be approved and
announced; and
(e) whether Government would clear
Rs. 16978.69 crores relief package for
farmers in 31 districts across four States
plagued by distress deaths
